title: Chapter 55
content:
Lathering a fresh dollop of shaving cream along his jaw, Il-hyun grimaced into the mirror.

Perhaps it was the overcast, drizzly weather, but a dull, electric ache pulsed through his right thigh as he stood. Nearly a year had passed since the assassination attempt, yet whenever the sky turned gray, that phantom sting flared to life.

For all their boasts about boasting the finest surgical talent in the country, Kang Yu-jung’s hospital staff had delivered a rather mediocre result. If they didn't share the same blood, he would have dragged them through the courts for malpractice and bled them dry in damages.

Finishing his shave, he took a brisk shower and stepped into the dressing room. Selecting a crisp dress shirt, a tailored silk tie, and a luxury timepiece, he fastened each in place before checking his reflection in the full-length mirror.

During the months Il-hyun spent recovering from his leg injury, Chairman Kang had formally promoted him to President and CEO of Haewon Group. Knowing he couldn't simply purge his lethal illegitimate son in one clean sweep, the old man had opted for theatrical appeasement—flattering him with titles while quietly lying in wait for the next vulnerability. A sly, treacherous old serpent to the very end.

Straightening the knot of his crimson-accented tie, Il-hyun descended the grand staircase, where Park Tae-soo was already waiting in the foyer.

"Good morning, President Kang."

Acknowledging the greeting, Il-hyun exchanged pleasantries with the morning staff and settled at the dining table. The senior housekeeper had prepared a fresh bowl of clear blowfish soup to soothe his stomach after last night's late-night drinks. Skipping the steamed rice, he lifted a spoonful of the hot, fragrant broth; the clean citrus notes immediately cleared the fog from his head.

"Working even on a Sunday, sir?" she asked, eyeing him with genuine maternal concern.

Lately, Il-hyun seemed consumed by his corporate empire. While an executive promotion naturally demanded long hours, skipping meals had become far too frequent, leaving her constantly worried for his health.

"Yes. I had unfinished business left over from yesterday."

"Shall I pack a lunchbox for your afternoon?"

"No need, ma'am. I'll grab something near the office."

Just then, the phone in Tae-soo's pocket vibrated.

Tae-soo stepped toward the living room to take the call. A few clipped murmurs followed—Yes. Understood.—before he hung up and returned to the dining room. His stoic face was loaded with unsaid words, but knowing better than to interrupt the President’s breakfast, he held his silence.Il-hyun lowered his spoon, looking up. "What is it?"

"A notification arrived from the parish shelter, sir."

"The shelter?"

Il-hyun’s hand paused over his water glass. Tae-soo kept his mouth shut, allowing the silence to speak.

Their gazes locked across the table. Slowly, a genuine, radiant smile spread across Kang Il-hyun’s handsome face.

He pushed his chair back and rose to his feet.

"Are you finished already, sir?" the housekeeper asked, surprised.

"Something urgent has come up."

Il-hyun strode toward the foyer with Tae-soo, pausing with his hand on the heavy double doors to look back over his shoulder.

"Ma'am."

"Yes, President Kang?"

His dark eyes gleamed with pure, boyish delight.

"Take extra care preparing dinner tomorrow evening. I have a feeling... a very precious guest will be arriving."

Dressed only in swim trunks, Jakyeong sprawled across a sun lounger, soaking in the tropical heat.

Out in the turquoise basin of the private pool, Wang Han, Rita, and Sasha were splashing about, batting an inflatable beach ball back and forth with lively laughter.

After a while, Sasha hoisted herself onto the tiled deck, toweled off, and plucked a chilled beer from the ice bucket, walking it over to his lounger.

"Thank you."

Jakyeong pushed himself up, taking a cold, satisfying pull from the bottle. Wang Han’s stray beach ball came arcing toward his head; Jakyeong swatted it back with an easy flick of his wrist, chuckling.

Sasha settled on the foot of his lounger, holding out a bottle of tanning oil with an expectant tilt of her chin.

"Rub some on my back?"

Her blue eyes crinkled with deep, charming dimples as she stretched out face-down on the canvas, undoing the back straps of her bikini top.

Jakyeong poured the oil into his palms, smoothing the slick warmth over her shoulders and spine. Her pale, alabaster skin seemed almost immune to the tropical sun—flushing a tender pink around the edges, but remaining just as fair as the day they met.

Her skin was remarkably soft beneath his calloused palms. As his hands worked down toward the small of her back, Sasha turned her head, fixing a heavy, unblinking gaze onto his face. Jakyeong deliberately ignored the unspoken invitation in those bright blue eyes.

Wang Han had been relentlessly nudging him lately, urging him to pursue something real with the girl. But with plans to relocate soon, entangling himself in casual romances felt like a needless distraction.

"Wei," she whispered, using his Chinese alias.

Jakyeong looked down as she dropped her voice to a conspiratorial murmur. "Just between you and me... Rita is totally in love with Han."

Jakyeong glanced toward the water. It was blindingly obvious; using the beach ball as an excuse, the two were practically wrapped around each other in the shallow end.

Watching them laugh, Jakyeong smiled, only for Sasha to nudge his knee.

"What about you?"

"What about me?"

"Is there someone you like?"

"Why ask that out of the blue?"

"You never seem interested in women," she teased, resting her chin on her crossed forearms. "I was starting to wonder if you preferred men."

Jakyeong gave a firm, unhesitating shake of his head. "Not in the slightest."

Hearing the instant denial, the corners of Sasha’s mouth curved into a delighted, sultry grin.

Before the conversation could drift further, Wang Han shouted from the pool, asking if Jakyeong could grab the electric air pump from the master suite to inflate the floaties.

Glad for the excuse, Jakyeong stood and padded inside the air-conditioned villa.

The muffled sounds of laughter drifted from the patio. Seeing Han so genuinely unburdened lately had Jakyeong privately wondering if spending the rest of his days in quiet exile like this wouldn't be half bad.

He stepped into the master bedroom, rummaging through the wardrobe for the pump when the floorboards creaked behind him.

He turned to find Sasha leaning against the closed door, looking breathtakingly pretty.

"They started kissing out there," she whispered with an innocent pout. "I figured I should give them some privacy."

She glided across the hardwood, dropping into a crouch right before him. "Need help finding it?"

Offering to help look while leaning your face in.

Her transparent game brought an amused smirk to Jakyeong's lips. Her upper body leaned in close, her soft, pillowy lips brushing against his.

Jakyeong didn't pull away. He parted his lips slightly, capturing hers in a gentle, rolling kiss.

Sasha pressed flush against his bare chest. With neither of them wearing shirts, the friction of bare skin against skin sent a slow, intoxicating warmth radiating through his veins. It was the first time in nearly a full year he had touched or kissed another human being—and the fresh, floral scent of her hair was undeniably sweet.

With a light buzz of alcohol in his blood and the natural instincts of a healthy young man, his body began heating up. His hand slid around her waist, fingertips grazing the loosened straps of her swimwear.

Buzz. Buzz.

The sharp vibration of his phone buzzing against the nightstand shattered the haze.

Jakyeong broke the kiss, placing a gentle hand on Sasha’s bare shoulder. She pulled back with an audible pop, her blue eyes filled with reluctant disappointment.

"Can't you answer that later?"

"Sorry. Just a second." It could be Wang Ryun checking in from Tokyo; ignoring operational channels was out of the question.

He stepped over to the mattress and scooped up the burner device. It was an international call from an unlisted number. When he accepted the line, the screen flickered into an incoming video feed. Assuming Ryun was using a secondary encrypted network, he waited for the video to buffer.

The screen stabilized, revealing a patch of clear blue sky followed by the tailored lapel of a dark suit.

What the hell?

Jakyeong’s brow furrowed.

A heartbeat later, the lens snapped into focus, framing a face he had spent twelve months trying to erase from his memory.

Jakyeong’s pupils dilated in absolute, paralyzing horror.

Resting a cigarette between his lips, Kang Il-hyun offered a radiant, dazzling smile straight into the camera.

[Hello, darling.]

In a sheer surge of primal panic, Jakyeong severed the call and hurled the phone across the duvet.

He stood frozen in the center of the bedroom like a petrified statue. Sasha approached, asking what was wrong, but the air caught in his throat. Did I hallucinate? No. That face was unmistakably Kang Il-hyun.

Before his racing pulse could slow, the phone buzzed against the sheets again. He stared at the screen as it vibrated relentlessly.

"Wei? Are you alright?" Sasha asked, reaching for his arm.

Jakyeong forced a stiff, hollow nod. He needed to find Wang Han immediately and initiate an emergency tactical evacuation.

Just as he turned toward the door, the device chimed again.

This time, the caller ID flashed Wang Ryun.

An icy dread clamped onto the base of Jakyeong’s skull.

He picked up the phone. It was another incoming video request. He pressed the accept key with trembling fingers.

The feed connected—and Kang Il-hyun’s face filled the screen once more.

God damn it.

Jakyeong closed his eyes for a split second, taking a ragged breath. The mocking, playful grin had vanished from Il-hyun's face, replaced by an arctic, unblinking stillness.

Suddenly remembering Sasha was standing bare inches away in nothing but unstrapped swimwear, Jakyeong angled the camera away, shoved the girl gently out into the hallway, and locked the bedroom door behind her.

Il-hyun’s lips twitched upward into a dark, venomous smirk.

[Looks like you're having quite the lovely vacation. Stripped completely naked, no less.]

Jakyeong ground his teeth, glaring through the screen.

Il-hyun lowered his dark lashes, then slowly raised them, his eyes brimming with a lethal, suffocating malice.

[I believe you and I still have unfinished business to settle.]

Jakyeong kept his silence, his knuckles turning white around the chassis.

[So tell me... Should I fly out there to collect you? Or are you going to walk back to me yourself?]

"Where is the owner of that phone?" Jakyeong demanded, his voice dropping into a harsh rasp.

Il-hyun arched a single brow. [This fellow?]

He flipped the rear camera.

Kneeling on a blood-slicked concrete floor was Wang Ryun—battered, broken, and drenched in arterial crimson.

Ryun forced his swollen eyelids open, desperately lunging toward the camera as he screamed with the last shred of breath in his lungs:

[D-Don't come! Ja-kyeong, stay the fuck away!]

Before Ryun could finish the shout, Il-hyun’s hand shot out, catching Ryun’s wrist in a vise grip and dragging the mangled hand toward his mouth.

Jakyeong’s breath hitched in sheer horror.

In a single, fluid snap, Il-hyun shoved Ryun’s pinky finger between his molars and bit down with monstrous force. A sickening snap of severed bone echoed through the speaker, followed by a blood-curdling, agonized shriek that tore straight through the microphone.

[Aaaaagh!]

Jakyeong stood paralyzed, staring in pure shock.

On screen, Kang Il-hyun casually extended his tongue. Resting flat across the pink muscle was the severed, bloody tip of Wang Ryun’s pinky finger.

Il-hyun picked the chunk of flesh off his tongue with his fingers, holding it up close to the camera lens with a wide, terrifying grin. The ragged edges of torn muscle and bone were rendered in gruesome high-definition.

"You sadistic piece of shit...!" Jakyeong hissed through ground teeth, his voice shaking with pure, unadulterated venom.

Il-hyun wiped the smear of blood from his lips with the back of his hand, fixing his pitch-black eyes straight down the barrel of the camera.

[Answer the question.]

The temperature in the bedroom seemed to plunge into absolute zero. Jakyeong stood motionless, chest heaving as he stared at the monster on the screen. A full year had passed, yet the man hadn't changed a single fraction of an inch—in fact, the murderous hunger in those eyes burned far hotter than ever before.

When Jakyeong failed to answer, Il-hyun tilted his head, asking the question one last time:

[Should I come to you... or are you coming back to me?]

Translator's Notes (A/N):

  • Bok-jiri (복지리탕): A clear, delicate soup made from fresh blowfish (fugu), white radish, water dropwort, and bean sprouts, traditionally prized in high-end Korean culinary circles as the ultimate restorative hangover cure for the wealthy after a night of heavy drinking.
